Both are late-administration letters from Truman to President-elect Eisenhower transmitting unfinished executive-branch work, explaining its origin and practical significance, distinguishing action that remains for the incoming President, and expressly calling the matter to Eisenhower's attention for consideration. C01 shares the transition-of-administration and completed-report setting but lacks the same addressee and close transmission-and-recommendation structure. C22 is only a generic acknowledgment of a transmitted report.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am glad to transmit to you the report ... which was handed to me ... others can be accomplished by the Executive Branch but would require the approval of the Chief Executive.","parent_excerpt":"I am forwarding herewith the draft of an Executive Order ... which has recently been developed and has come to me for approval. I am deferring issuance of the Order...","explanation":"Both transmit a recently completed executive proposal to the President-elect because consequential executive approval or action remains pending."},{"child_excerpt":"At my request this Committee investigated fully the procedures now being used... The Committee report submits a total of twenty-two recommendations...","parent_excerpt":"The proposed Order is the result of many months' study by experts in the Civil Service Commission and the Bureau of the Budget.","explanation":"Each briefly establishes that the enclosed work resulted from substantial executive-branch study before recommending it to the incoming administration."},{"child_excerpt":"I feel the Committee has done a thorough job of investigation and I wish to call your attention to these suggestions, some of which, I am sure, would be helpful.","parent_excerpt":"I believe it is of such importance that I am calling it to your attention as being in the best interests of the Federal civil service.","explanation":"The distinctive concluding formulation—affirming the work's merit and 'calling it to your attention'—is closely parallel and serves the same persuasive function."}]}
